# Dialog

> A dialog built on the native `<dialog>`, modal or not. A modal one keeps focus inside, closes on Escape, and makes the rest of the page inert — the platform does the heavy lifting.

`<slab-dialog>` · Overlays · built on `<dialog>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/dialog/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/dialog.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-dialog label="Delete this file?">
  <p>It can't be recovered.</p>

  <form method="dialog">
    <button value="cancel">Cancel</button>
    <button value="delete">Delete</button>
  </form>
</slab-dialog>
```

Open it with `showModal()`. When it closes, `returnValue` tells you which
button did it — same as a `<dialog>`.

## Modal or not

Calling `showModal()` opens it as a modal. Calling `show()`, or setting `open`,
opens it non-modally, the way they open a `<dialog>`: there's no backdrop,
focus can leave it, and the rest of the page stays usable while it's open.

```js
const dialog = document.querySelector('slab-dialog');

dialog.showModal(); // The rest of the page goes inert.
dialog.show(); // The rest of the page stays usable.
```

A `<dialog>` can't be opened as a modal without script, so Slab adds `modal`.
With it, setting `open` opens it as `showModal()` does, which is what a
framework that binds `open` needs. `show()` and `showModal()` still open it as
they say.

```html
<slab-dialog label="Delete this file?" modal open>…</slab-dialog>
```

As with a `<dialog>`, Escape only closes a non-modal one with `closedby`. Set
`closedby="closerequest"` for Escape, or `closedby="any"` for a click outside
it too. Style one or the other with `::part(dialog):modal` and
`::part(dialog):not(:modal)`.

## Keyboard

| Key            | What it does                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Moves focus between the dialog's controls. When it's modal, the rest of the page is inert.                          |
| Escape         | Closes the dialog and dispatches "cancel", which can be canceled to keep it open. A non-modal one needs `closedby`. |

## Elements

### `<slab-dialog>`

Import `slab-elements/dialog.js` to register it.

A dialog with no visual styles, around a native `<dialog>`, opened modally or not the way one is.

`showModal()` opens it as a modal: it traps focus, closes on Escape, has a `::backdrop`, and makes the rest of the page inert. `show()`, or setting `open`, opens it non-modally, as they open a `<dialog>`: the rest of the page stays interactive, there's no backdrop, and, as natively, Escape only closes it with `closedby`. Calling either method while it's open leaves it as it is. Match a modal one with `::part(dialog):modal`.

`modal` is Slab's, for a modal opened declaratively, as a framework binding `open` does: with it, setting `open` opens it as `showModal()` does.

`open` reflects, and it stays true to the dialog: when the dialog closes itself, on Escape or through a `<form method="dialog">`, `open` goes false along with it. `close(returnValue)` and a `<form method="dialog">`'s submitter both set `returnValue`, as they do on a `<dialog>`.

The dialog is named by its label: the `label` attribute or the `label` slot. The label isn't a heading, because a heading's level is the page's to choose. Plain `label` text names the dialog without being one. For a heading, slot your own at whatever level fits: `<h2 slot="label">`.

Light dismiss is the platform's or nothing. `closedby="any"` is passed through to the `<dialog>`, which closes on a backdrop click where the browser supports it and ignores the attribute where it doesn't. Nothing here listens for clicks on the backdrop to fake it.

Style it through its parts, and the backdrop through `::part(dialog)::backdrop`.

#### Attributes

| Name         | Type                                | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `closedby`   | `'any' \| 'closerequest' \| 'none'` |         | Passed to the `<dialog>`. "any" closes it on a click outside it where the browser supports that. Browsers that don't ignore it.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `hide-label` | `boolean`                           | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `label`      | `string`                            |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `modal`      | `boolean`                           | `false` | Opens it as a modal when `open` is set, as `showModal()` does, for a modal opened declaratively. Not on a native `<dialog>`, where `open` always opens a non-modal one. `show()` and `showModal()` open it as they say whatever it is, and a change while it's open waits for it to open again. |
| `open`       | `boolean`                           | `false` | Whether it's open. Setting it opens it non-modally, as `open` does on a `<dialog>`, unless `modal` is set.                                                                                                                                                                                      |

#### Properties

| Name          | Type     | Description                                                                                               |
| ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `returnValue` | `string` | The `<dialog>`'s, so `close(returnValue)` and a `<form method="dialog">` set it the way they do natively. |

#### Methods

| Signature                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close(returnValue?: string): void`        | Closes it, setting `returnValue` to the value given, as a native dialog's `close()` does.                                                                           |
| `requestClose(returnValue?: string): void` | Asks it to close, as a native dialog's `requestClose()` does: "cancel" first, then a close that sets `returnValue` to the value given, unless "cancel" is canceled. |
| `show(): void`                             | Opens it non-modally, as a native dialog's `show()` does, whether or not `modal` is set. The rest of the page stays interactive.                                    |
| `showModal(): void`                        | Opens it as a modal, as a native dialog's `showModal()` does, whether or not `modal` is set.                                                                        |

#### Events

| Name     | Type          | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancel` | `Event`       | When something asks it to close: Escape, a click outside with `closedby="any"`, or `requestClose()`. Cancel it to keep it open, as a native dialog's. |
| `toggle` | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does.                                  |
| `close`  | `Event`       | When it closes, as a native dialog's does.                                                                                                            |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                      |
| --------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `label`   | `Element \| string` | Its heading, in place of `label` |
| (default) | `Element \| string` |                                  |

#### CSS parts

| Name     | Description                                                 |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialog` | The native dialog. A modal one's backdrop is its ::backdrop |
| `label`  | The label                                                   |

#### CSS states

| Name           | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| `:state(open)` | While it's open. |
